summary: Abe proves Serre's conjecture on the higher-dimensional Artin character in equal characteristic: for a regular local ring containing a finite field with an admissible finite group action, a_G is the character of a Qℓ-rational representation. The proof reduces, by Kato–Saito–Saito, to a trace identity for a Fourier nearby cycle (Theorem 1.6), obtained from Lu–Zheng's relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace after a universally locally acyclic extension over an alteration (Theorem 1.5), and compares that nearby cycle with Laumon's total-dimension representation (Proposition 2.5) to get Qℓ-rationality. 110 items (12 library, 8 planned, 90 missing) are routed to EDC.8 and LPV.0 and to four Part IIs (equivariant traces, relative traces, general-base Fourier, geometric Artin representations). Six findings are recorded, all in the arXiv v2 text as well: a fixed-scheme identification in the proof of Theorem 1.6 (E3), the coefficient scope of the Lu–Zheng citation (E4), and four slips in the concluding remarks (E1, E2, E5, E6). Independent review confirms all six source findings and accepts the six ownership routes after correction, but restores partial status: twelve supplier obligations remain open or unavailable.

conventions.C1: A is a regular local ring with maximal ideal m and finite group G acting by local automorphisms. A^G is Noetherian, A is finite over A^G, A/Iσ has finite length for every σ≠1, Iσ=(a−σ(a):a∈A), and A^G/(m∩A^G)→A/m is an isomorphism. The main theorem additionally assumes A contains a finite field, hence characteristic p>0; ℓ is invertible in A.
conventions.C2: In the geometric theorem k is algebraically closed of characteristic p>0, ℓ≠p, S is the strict henselization of P¹_t at 0, S′ that of P¹_t′ at ∞′, and η′ its generic point. f:X→S is flat of finite type, X regular, G finite acting by S-automorphisms, the union of the fixed loci for nonidentity elements has underlying set {x}, and f is smooth outside the closed point x. Λ=Qℓ(ζp), with a fixed nontrivial ψ:Fp→Λ×. Nearby-cycle complexes and traces are unshifted cohomological objects; traces mean alternating traces.
conventions.C3: For ramification modules K=Frac(k{t}) with k algebraically closed of characteristic p>0, Γ=Gal(Ksep/K), ℓ≠p, G finite commuting with Γ. A chosen Galois tower and compatible isomorphisms of Swan modules are data at integral level. They are not declared canonical. Rational coefficients L are finite extensions of Qℓ. This is the hypothesis in §2.2. The separably closed field mentioned separately in §3.1 is not used to enlarge the Swan construction without proving the additional ramification hypotheses.
conventions.C4: Dctf means constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension. For the cited Lu–Zheng dualizability theorem use a Noetherian commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer invertible on the Noetherian base. Actual Theorem 1.5 and finite-level trace application use finite rings; no unchecked extension to arbitrary non-Noetherian coefficients is claimed.
conventions.C5: RL(G) is K0 of perfect L[G]-complexes. In characteristic zero it is compared to the existing split representation ring via semisimplicity and Euler characteristic, not identified by notation alone. DΛ-perf(Λ[G]) means perfect over Λ, not necessarily over Λ[G].
conventions.C6: All library citations are exact existing carriers/theorems only. Added planning API and tests are specifications for reuse/adapters, not claims that wrappers or the paper are formalized. Items depend on the conventions and the explicitly named gap gates as well as their item dependencies.

items.name: Regular-character ambiguity in a nonidentity trace identity
items.statement: For a finite group G over a characteristic-zero field, adding a multiple of the regular character changes only the value at 1. Therefore the nonidentity trace formula alone does not fix the normalized identity value, positivity or rational descent.

items.statement: For a tower of finite separable smooth curve germs X→qY→gS over an algebraically closed field, d(f)=d(q)+e(q)d(g), where d is the local different exponent and e the ramification index. items.statement: In A20, the isolated fixed local algebra is Artinian with unchanged residue field, so its étale/strict-henselian base-change comparison preserves its length. proofSteps: The chosen base change is ind-étale with the selected closed fibre Spec(k). After passing to the local ring B′ over B, it is flat and satisfies m_B B′=m_B′ and B′/m_B B′=k. Take a composition series of the finite-length B-module B/Iσ. Tensor it with B′. Flatness preserves exactness and each simple factor becomes B′/m_BB′=k, a simple B′-module. Hence the full fixed length is unchanged.
This proves the needed numerical equality without identifying the Artinian fixed scheme with its closed fibre. The existence/spreading of B and the strict-local comparison remain in A20 and G-HENSEL.

proofSteps: Write A_n=S_n(M′), B_n=S_n(M), C_n=S_n(M″), D_n=ker(B_n→C_n), K_n=ker(A_n→B_n). These are finite modules, with 0→K_n→A_n→D_n→0 and 0→D_n→B_n→C_n→0 exact.

B19 implies lim K_n=0: the nth coordinate comes from the zero transition from n+c. Thus lim A_n≅lim D_n and the desired Swan sequence is exact. This accounts for reduction Tor kernels, rather than assuming they vanish termwise.

items.statement: Let Λ be a commutative finite projective Zℓ-algebra and M a finitely generated Λ-module with continuous action trivialized by the compatible Swan tower B04. items.name: Effectivity and finite generation of the Swan inverse system
items.statement: For Λ, M and S_n(M) under all the hypotheses of B17, S(M)=lim S_n(M) is finitely generated over Λ, is ℓ-adically complete, and S(M)/ℓ^n S(M)≅S_n(M), compatibly with the commuting finite G-action.
proofSteps: Choose generators of S_1 and lift them compatibly through the surjective transitions. They generate S_n over Λ/ℓ^n by Nakayama.
The finite kernels K_n of (Λ/ℓ^n)^r→S_n have surjective transition maps: correct any lift using ker(S_(n+1)→S_n)=ℓ^nS_(n+1).
Apply the finite-fibre section theorem to obtain Λ^r→lim S_n surjective; Λ is complete because it is finite projective over Zℓ. Taking kernels and their surjective reductions gives S/ℓ^nS≅S_n.

items.name: Reduction kernels in a Swan exact sequence become zero after a bounded transition
items.statement: For 0→M′→M→M″→0 of finite Λ-modules in the fixed-tower category, set E_n=ker(M′/ℓ^nM′→M/ℓ^nM). If ℓ^c kills the Zℓ-torsion of M″, every map E_(n+c)→E_n is zero. The corresponding finite Swan-kernel transition is zero as well.
proofSteps: Identify E_n with (M′∩ℓ^nM)/ℓ^nM′. If x=ℓ^(n+c)y lies in M′, the class of y in M″ is torsion, so ℓ^c y lies in M′ and x lies in ℓ^nM′.
Compute each comparison at a common sufficiently large quotient of the fixed tower. Exactness identifies the Swan kernel with sw(E_n), and functoriality sends the zero transition to zero.
The case M′=ℓ^cZℓ⊂M=Zℓ has nonzero E_n for c>0; termwise injectivity would be false.

The output is finite by B18; over the DVR O, ℓ-torsion-freeness implies torsion-freeness and hence freeness. Scalar annihilation is preserved by the linear finite-level functor and its limit.
